executable_actions.rationale: The supplied summary shows relevant artifact and constraint classes but not checker-bound numeric/template/parameter evidence. Run the stage-required static checks before promotion.

executable_actions.on_failure: If a gap cannot be repaired by binding existing supplied facts, stop the patch, keep the candidate blocked, and escalate to the approval-gated semantic resolution action.
executable_actions.rationale: If the audit finds facts present in supplied inputs but not explicitly bound in SACG, repair only those binding edges and boundary annotations; do not change numeric policy, template semantics, or design-space values in this action.

executable_actions.on_failure: Classify failures as current-stage SACG binding blockers when required facts are absent; otherwise record them as later-stage handoff risks with explicit constraints and do not claim hardware pass.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep the original candidate blocked for downstream consumption; do not update policy, template coverage, or design-space facts until approval is recorded and all current-stage static checks pass after the update.

proposed_actions: Run the numeric, template coverage, template binding, and parameter binding static checks over the candidate SACG and supplied input artifacts.

Produce artifact.review.constraint_extraction.numeric_template_findings, artifact.review.constraint_extraction.template_binding_gap_list, and artifact.review.constraint_extraction.parameter_binding_patch_requests as the bounded handoff to the constraint graph auditor.
If gaps are only missing SACG bindings to already supplied facts, create a bounded binding patch and rerun the same checkers before promotion.

If any gap requires changing numeric policy, adding/changing templates, changing design-space parameters, or altering memory/layout/runtime assumptions, require explicit approval before updating the SACG.

Record cross-layer handoff notes linking model/shape, numeric policy, template metadata, data order, memory/runtime, implementation resource risk, and board assumptions; keep hardware correctness unclaimed until later real tool evidence exists.

Template metadata and design-space parameters may not have explicit legal ranges, selected values, provenance, or binding boundaries, risking invalid generated configurations.

Resource-risk assumptions may not be bound from design-space choices to board memory, runtime transfer units, implementation resource budgets, and timing-risk thresholds; this should be treated as a cross-layer handoff risk until checked.

Data order and transfer-unit assumptions are not visible in the numeric/template summary; if packing order, stream order, or memory layout is inconsistent with numeric formats and template ports, later functional comparison can fail despite structurally valid SACG nodes.
Zero validation errors in the compact candidate summary can hide omitted checker evidence; do not claim pass or promote downstream consumption without the named checker artifacts.
